newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl calls crisis meeting for Expo 2000 - magazine.
newsitem.headline: Kohl calls crisis meeting for Expo 2000 - magazine.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl has called 45 German industrial leaders to a crisis meeting later this month to give a boost to the struggling Expo 2000 world fair in Hanover, a German magazine said on Wednesday.

The weekly business magazine Wirtschaftswoche said in an advance text of its next issue appearing on Thursday that only four German companies have so far expressed interest in sponsorships in the exposition.
"Industrial nations such as Japan, China and the United States have so far not given any commitments for participation," the magazine said.
Wirtschaftswoche said Kohl, who has taken a personal interest in the success of the Expo, had called industrialists to a meeting in the Chancellery in Bonn on October 23.

The Expo 2000 in Hanover is supposed to be a showcase for a new modern Germany, coming 10 years after the country's unification and at about the same time the government is planning to move from Bonn to Berlin.
